outcome.rationale: Novel mechanistic trial with biologically plausible interventions but no direct efficacy evidence in CAA. Primary CSF endpoint has mechanistic support but 3-month duration and pre-post design limit causal inference. Safety profile manageable. Trial likely to generate hypothesis-confirming data but definitive success uncertain.

value.estimand: LXB vs baseline at 3 months: change in CSF morning Aβ40/42 (pg/mL)
value.uncertainty: No direct CAA intervention trials; pre-post design; 3-month duration may be insufficient for measurable CSF changes; high inter-individual variability expected
value.rationale: Based on Dagum 2026 showing sleep enhances glymphatic Aβ clearance and Walsh 2010 showing sodium oxybate increases SWS. Predict modest CSF Aβ reduction with LXB. nVNS mechanism (CSD inhibition) less directly linked to CSF clearance. Combination may have additive effect. Low confidence due to lack of direct evidence in CAA population.

analysis_trace: Trial: NCT06421532 (Clear-Brain) is a Phase 2 randomized pre-post trial investigating glymphatic stimulation via low-sodium oxybate (LXB/XYWAV) and/or non-invasive vagus nerve stimulation (nVNS/gammaCore Sapphire) in cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) patients. Primary endpoint measures change in CSF Aβ40/42 levels at 3 months. Evidence from Dagum et al. (2026, Nat Commun) demonstrates that sleep-active glymphatic clearance increases morning plasma Aβ/tau levels in humans, supporting the mechanistic rationale. CSF biomarker studies (Sembill 2023, van den Berg 2024) show CAA patients have reduced CSF Aβ40/42 compared to controls. Sodium oxybate enhances slow-wave sleep (Walsh 2010), which drives glymphatic clearance. nVNS inhibits cortical spreading depression (PMC4943574). No direct efficacy data exists for these specific interventions in CAA. Safety data: gammaCore shows mild application-site AEs; sodium oxybate has known risks (sleep apnea, depression). Expected completion September 2027.

Evidence roles: Dagum 2026 (mechanism_background - glymphatic clearance in humans supports mechanism); Walsh 2010 (mechanism_background - sodium oxybate enhances SWS); Sembill 2023 (indirect_direction - CSF Aβ40/42 reduced in CAA, provides baseline context); van den Berg 2024 (indirect_direction - Aβ peptide profiles in CAA); gammaCore safety data (direct_numeric - application-site discomfort 2.5%, erythema/pain 2.4%).

Prediction approach: For primary CSF endpoint, predict modest reduction in morning Aβ40/42 with LXB due to enhanced clearance, minimal effect with nVNS alone, potential additive effect with combination. Confidence low due to lack of direct CAA intervention trials. For imaging endpoints, predict stabilization/slow progression given 3-month timeframe. For safety, predict typical sodium oxybate and nVNS adverse events.

Key uncertainties: No prior trials of LXB or nVNS in CAA; 3-month duration may be insufficient for structural imaging changes; pre-post design limits causal inference; BATMAN control group mentioned but not fully characterized.
